## Variables

### DBH

```{r}
summary(forestry.all$DBH)
```

```{r}
par(mfrow=c(1,2), bg = "gray40")
hist(forestry.all |> filter(DBH < 100 & DBH > 0) |> pull(DBH),main = "DBH Histogram", xlab = "Diameter at Breast Height", col = "gray60")
boxplot(forestry.all |> filter(DBH < 100 & DBH > 0) |> pull(DBH),main = "DBH Boxplot", ylab = "Diameter at Breast Height", col = "gray60")
```



```{r}
forestry.all |> filter(DBH < 0)
```

```{r}
forestry.all |> filter(DBH > 100) |> select(SCI_NM, DBH)
```

### MBG Width

```{r}
par(mfrow=c(1,2), bg = "gray40")
hist(forestry.all |> pull(MBG_WIDTH),main = "MBG Width Histogram", xlab = "Horizontal Measure of Foliage and Branches", col = "gray60")
boxplot(forestry.all |> pull(MBG_WIDTH),main = "MBG Width Boxplot", ylab = "Horizontal Measure of Foliage and Branches", pch = "+", col = "gray60")
```

### MBG Length

```{r}
par(mfrow=c(1,2), bg = "gray40")
hist(forestry.all |> pull(MBG_LENGTH),main = "MBG Length Histogram", xlab = "Vertical Measure from top to live crown", col = "gray60")
boxplot(forestry.all |> pull(MBG_LENGTH),main = "MBG Length Boxplot", ylab = "Vertical Measure from top to live crown", pch = "+", col = "gray60")
```

### Max Mean

```{r}
par(mfrow=c(1,2), bg = "gray40")
hist(forestry.all |> pull(MAX_MEAN),main = "Max Mean Histogram", xlab = "Avg vert dist from base to the live crown", col = "gray60")
boxplot(forestry.all |> pull(MAX_MEAN),main = "Max Mean Boxplot", ylab = "Avg vert dist from base to the live crown", pch = "+", col = "gray60")
```

### Max Crown Height

```{r}
par(mfrow=c(1,2), bg = "gray40")
hist(forestry.all |> pull(MAX_CROWN_HEIGHT),main = "Max Crown Height Histogram", xlab = "Vert dist from lowest live branch to apex", col = "gray60")
boxplot(forestry.all |> pull(MAX_CROWN_HEIGHT),main = "Max Crown Height Boxplot", ylab = "Vert dist from lowest live branch to apex", pch = "+", col = "gray60")
```


### TBOX_L

```{r}
par(mfrow=c(1,2), bg = "gray40")
hist(forestry.all |> pull(TBOX_L),main = "Max Crown Height Histogram", xlab = "Vert dist from lowest live branch to apex", col = "gray60")
boxplot(forestry.all |> pull(TBOX_L),main = "Max Crown Height Boxplot", ylab = "Vert dist from lowest live branch to apex", pch = "+", col = "gray60")
```

## Extreme Value

```{r}
extreme_value <- forestry.all |> 
  select(SCI_NM,TBOX_L, GLOBALID, OBJECTID, LAST_EDITED_DATE) |> 
  arrange(desc(TBOX_L)) |> head(1)
extreme_value
```

```{r}
extreme_value |> kableExtra::kable() |> kableExtra::kable_styling()
```

## Appendix

### RETIREDDT

This variable basically informs us that there are two separate data sets we should work with. The living trees, and the dead ones.

Only 5452 trees are alive. The rest have been "retired".

```{r}
livetrees <- forestry.all |> filter(RETIREDDT != "NA")
nrow(livetrees)
```

```{r}
colSums(is.na(forestry.all))
```

### NA Column Totals

```{r}
forestry.all |> 
  summarize(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.)))) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), 
               names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  filter(value > 100000)
```


```{r}
colSums(is.na(forestry.all))
```



```{r}
forestry.numeric |> select(MBG_WIDTH, MBG_LENGTH) -> forestry.pairs
cor(forestry.pairs)
```


```{r}
par( bg="gray40", col="gray10")
plot(forestry.all$X, forestry.all$Y, pch="+")
```


```{r}
forestry.all %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.))))
```

We may have to just use the subset of trees that have a created date, and then see when they died to create a new variable such as longevity.

```{r}
forestry.all |> select(CREATED_DATE) |> distinct()
```

This variable must exclude the live trees. We don't know how long they will live for because they're still alive.
